text:
emma: FYI customer ryan hit a tool-call failure when passing nested JSON as arguments to a function call. Error says schema validation failed (expected object, got string)

ryan: Repro steps I gave them: Python SDK -> call tool with a dict arg, TS SDK -> call from frontend. Python works, TS fails. Here's what we saw from client side.

ryan: ```python
# python snippet (works)
tool_call = {
  "name": "lookup_user",
  "arguments": {"query": {"id": "123", "meta": {"flag": true}}}
}
client.call_tool(tool_call)
```

ryan: ```ts
// typescript snippet (failing)
const args = { query: { id: '123', meta: { flag: true } } }
// not sure why this ended up as a string in the request body
client.callTool('lookup_user', JSON.stringify(args))
```

emma: Server error response captured: ```json
{
  "error": "tool_invocation_failed",
  "details": "arguments: invalid type: string for field 'query'"
}
```

ling: This reads like double-encoding on the client: server expects the `arguments` field to be an object matching the tool schema but received a string. Can you paste the raw HTTP request body from the failing TS call (or the SDK logs)?

ryan: Pulled the network trace, body was: ```json
{
  "name": "lookup_user",
  "arguments": "{\"query\":{\"id\":\"123\",\"meta\":{\"flag\":true}}}"
}
```

charlie: aha — arguments is a JSON-encoded string in the payload. That would pass in Python (which sends a native object) but TS code above explicitly stringified. But you said they didn't intentionally stringify?

ryan: They didn't on purpose — they pass a template into a helper that sometimes returns a stringified JSON (we found a sanitize helper that does this for certain payload shapes). Edge-case.

ling: Two things to consider: (1) server used to accept both object and string but a validation tightening in the last release rejects string now (we pushed stricter function schema validation), (2) TS SDK helper should avoid implicit stringify or at least warn.

emma: SDK versions: python-sdk 1.3.2, ts-sdk 1.1.9, go-sdk 0.9.0. Customer running ts 1.1.9.

ling: Can you reproduce with curl? If curl with object succeeds and with encoded string fails, then it's client-side.

emma: Repro with curl posted: success when sending object, fail when sending encoded string.

emma: ```bash
# works
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/call -d '{"name":"lookup_user","arguments":{"query":{"id":"123"}}}'
# fails (arguments as string)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/call -d '{"name":"lookup_user","arguments":"{\"query\":{\"id\":\"123\"}}"}'
```

deploy-bot: candidate/2026-03-12 reverted: validation-strict-mode -> rolled back (reason: broke TS SDK consumers)

ling: Root cause summary: new server-side strict validation rejects JSON-encoded strings for `arguments`. Some client helpers in TS/Go implicitly stringify certain structures (templating/sanitizers).

charlie: Proposed immediate mitigations: (A) support can un-stringify arguments for affected customers on the proxy layer (quick fix), (B) revert strict validation (already rolled back), (C) patch TS/Go SDK helpers to avoid stringify and add guard/console.warn.

emma: Opened support ticket SUP-2026-478 and toggled customer to lenient validation scope while we patch. Customer accepts workaround.

ling: Next steps: Devex to ship TS SDK patch that checks `typeof args === 'string'` and JSON.parse if intentionally passing string, but prefer to keep API expecting object. Add a warning log when string detected. Also add a unit test for nested JSON shapes.

charlie: I'll draft PR for SDK and link to SUP-2026-478. ETA for patch: ~24h.

ryan: Thanks everyone. Will confirm when customer verifies.

emma: closing once SDK patch is released and customer confirms — leaving thread open until then.
